So, we were founded just over ten years ago, when I was in the Royal Academy, a Museum in the centre of London, with my three children, at the Aztec exhibition. I don’t know if any of you saw it. I had an older child and two younger children, twins, strapped in a pushchair, and one of my children, three years old, shouted–and I’ve never denied he shouted–he shouted, ‘Monster, monster!’ at this statue which looked just like a monster, had snakes for hair, a big beak for a nose. And, I thought, this is fantastic–I’ve got a three-year old that’s appreciating pre-Hispanic art–how good can it get? So, I bent down and I said, ‘Yes, it looks just like a monster’. And, at that moment, a room warden came over, a gallery assistant came over and said we were being too noisy, and threw us out. Wrong family. I was, at that time, a journalist with The Guardian newspaper, and two days later wrote a big piece in The Guardian about being thrown out of the Royal Academy. What was really interesting was, by the end of that day, we had had, at the paper, over 500 emails from other families saying, ‘Museums aren’t working for us. Let’s try and make it work’. So, that’s what we did. In The Guardian, we set up a campaign. We called it the Kids in Museums campaign, but it didn’t really exist. It was just a few pages. We ran loads of stories on it; I began touring the country talking about how to make your museum family friendly; I was a journalist. I was called in to see the then director of the National Gallery in London, and I’ll never forget this moment, when he called me in and said, ‘We really like this Kids in Museums campaign, and we’ve been talking on our board about it, and we have some ideas of how we might work together, and I’d like you to take them back to your team.

Language death is not mainstream theatre. It is not mainstream anything. Can you imagine Hollywood taking it on? It is so far outside the mindsets of most people that they have a difficulty appreciating what the crisis is all about, because they are not used to thinking more about language as an issue in itself. Somehow, we need to change these mindsets. We need to get people thinking more about language more explicitly, more intimately, more enthusiastically. Interest in language is certainly there, in the general population. Most people are fascinated by such topics as where words come from, or what the origin of their town’s name is, or whether their baby’s name means anything; they are certainly prepared to play Scrabble and a host of other language games and infinitum ( 无限地, 无穷大); and you get language games on radio and television too – but a willingness to focus that interest on general issues, a preparedness to take on board the emotion and drama inherent in the situation of language endangerment, is not something that happens much.

Normally, however, spectacles are part of an assemblage of items, giving us an overall ‘look’. In fashion terms, they are classed as ‘accessories’ along with shoes, jewellery, handbags or watches. Choosing your spectacles is therefore a major decision. Increasingly people own two or more pairs for different occasions or times of the day. There is a phrase for this in the industry. And I am the professor of children's literature at Newcastle University. And I want to write a very short introduction to children's literature because although, here in Britain, we have one of the longest and most distinguished traditions of creating books for children, perhaps the longest and most distinguished in the world, we often take them for granted and we don't pay enough attention to what a remarkable cultural resource they are for adults and the kind of cultural work they do for children and the way that they have served writers and illustrators as a cultural space for creativity subversion and opportunities to experiment with new ideas.

So what kind of cultural work the children's books do? Well, at the level of individual child, this is one of the places where children learn the vocabularies, get the vicarious experiences, and see the images of the world that help them think about how the world works and where they fit into it. Because children's books are one of the first places that children encounter these things, they are often very direct as a source of information about what a particular period thinks, including what it thinks a child is, what a child needs to know, what childhood looks like. Sometimes when we are looking at children's books from the past, that's very important to notice the kinds of children who aren't there, for instance. So, that is one of the things that we have in children's books.

What is globalization? And I think that it takes on a few different definitions.

international communications, more trade happening between countries and be less self-sufficient in providing goods and services to their people and more companies that have offices in multiple countries, which we call multinationals. So, the source of growth in travel and communication and corporate spread across borders. And this way of thinking about globalization is a continuation of thinking that has been around for a long time, such as when the Europeans went to the Orient, to find spices, which was also an example of global trade and communication.

Another way to think of globalization though, is as an economic system. It is a system in which countries become integrated in a way that never had been before. In this system, we see a global split in the process between consuming and producing goods. Some countries produce goods, some countries consume goods, and then these countries in different areas of the globe depend on each other in a kind of organic solidarity rather than having an economic system being just inside your country. 权力下放是指将权力从联邦下方到州一级，也就是将权力下放到普通公众。

The Democrats believe in big government.
哲学上的问题是，民主党人相信大政府和中央集权，而共和党人相信权力应该更是给予人民和州级别的，因为他们是民粹主义者。

然而，权力的下放其实是把权力从人民手中拿走，因为权力体系中有一个隐藏的部分，那就是私有权力。

blocks.p: Devolution means reducing and modifying power from the Federal to State level, lowering power to the general public The philosophical issue is that the Democrats believe in big government and entitlements, and the Republicans believe in getting power down closer to people and states because they’ re populist types However, devolution is moving power away from the people because there’s a hidden part of the power system which’s private power
Well, that’s one aspect of what’s called, reducing government — modifying government, to be more precise.

Another aspect of it is what’s called “devolution” — reducing — moving governmental power from the Federal to the State level. And that has a kind of a rationale which you hear all over the time — place. For example, there was XXXXX a couple of weeks ago in the New York Times by John Cogan — Hoover Institute at Stanford, who’s pointed out what he called a philosophical issue that divides the Democrats from the Republicans. The philosophical issue is that the Democrats believe in big government and entitlements, and the Republicans believe in getting power down closer to the people, to the States because they’re kind of populist types.

Well, it takes about maybe three seconds’ thought to recognize, to realize that moving power down to the States, in funding and so on, is just moving it away from the people, for a perfectly elementary reason: there’s a hidden part of the system — of the power system that you’re not supposed to know about, or think about, and that’s private power.

SST.title: Faults and Earthquakes 地震与断层

sections.label: 简化版答案 · 中英对照（建议 7 炸以下背这版）

pairs: Faults are breaks in the earth’s crust, and earthquakes occur on these faults.
断层是地壳的破裂，地震就发生在这些断层之上。
The earthquake starts at the particular point on the fault plane.
地震始于断层面上的某一点，我们称之为震源。
And that point is the focus of the earthquake.
岩石从破裂面上的该点向外延伸，进而覆盖整个断层面。

垂直于震源上方的震中，就是地震震源的表面投影。
The epicenter is vertically above the focus of the earthquake.

blocks.p: Faults are breaks in the earth’s crust, and earthquakes occur on these faults. The earthquake starts at the particular point on the fault plane and we call that the focus of the earthquake. The rock propagates out from that point on the rupture plane to cover the entire fault plane. The epicenter, vertically above that focus, is just the surface projection of the focus of the earthquake.

So, faults are breaks in the earth’s crust. We can identify them because of the discontinuity in the structure within the earth crust across fault. And earthquakes occur on these faults, so vary processes by which these faults move to a large extent is due to earthquakes.

So, we have a fault plane, and the earthquake is so focus on this fault plane and the earthquake starts at the particular point on the fault plane and we call that the focus of the earthquake. The rock propagates out from that point on the rupture plane to cover the entire fault plane. The rupture is in that particular earthquake.

We talked about the epicenter of the earthquake a lot. The epicenter is just the surface projection of the focus of the earthquake. So, if you wanted to look at map view where the earthquake was located, we would be able to look that into the earth. We would see the focus down some depth in the earth or the epicenter is just a point vertically above that focus at the surface of the earth. So, this is the relationship between the faults and earthquakes.

The earthquake starts at the particular point on the fault plane and we call that the focus of the earthquake.
The rock propagates out from that point on the rupture plane to cover the entire fault plane.
The epicenter, vertically above that focus, is just the surface projection of the focus of the earthquake.

SWT.title: Grass and Cow 牛和草

blocks.p: The co-evolutionary relationship between cows and grass is one of nature’s underappreciated wonders.

For the grasses, which have evolved to withstand the grazing of ruminants, the cow maintains and expands their habitat by preventing trees and shrubs from gaining a foothold and hogging the sunlight; the animal also spreads grass seed, plants it with his hooves, and then fertilizes it with his manure. In exchange for these services the grasses offer ruminants a plentiful and exclusive supply of lunch.

For cows (like sheep, bison, and other ruminants) have evolved the special ability to convert grass – which single-stomached creatures like us can’t digest – into high-quality protein. They can do this because they possess what is surely the most highly evolved digestive organ in nature: the rumen. About the size of a medicine ball, the organ is essentially a forty-five-gallon fermentation tank in which a resident population of bacteria dines on grass.

While the grasses have evolved to withstand the grazing of ruminants because the cow not only maintains and expands their habitat, but also spreads, plants and then fertilizes grass seeds, cows have evolved the special ability to convert grass into protein because they possess the most highly evolved digestive organ: the rumen in which a resident population of bacteria dines on grass, which is the co-evolutionary relationship between cows and grass.

SWT.title: Parent’s Born Order and Parenting Ver. 1 家长出生顺序版一

materials.title: Parent’s Born Order and Parenting Ver. 1

blocks.p: Parents' own born order can become an issue when dynamics in the family they are raising replicate the family in which they were raised. Agati notes common examples, such as a firstborn parent getting into "raging battles" with a firstborn child. "Both are used to getting the last word. Each has to be right. But the parent has to be the grown up and step out of that battle," he advises.

When youngest children become parents, Agati cautions that because they "may not have had high expectations placed on them, they in turn may not see their kids for their abilities." But he also notes that since youngest children tend to be more social, "youngest parents can be helpful to their firstborn, who may have a harder time with social situations. These parents can help their eldest kids loosen up and not be so hard on themselves.

Mom Susan Ritz says her own birth order didn't seem to affect her parenting until the youngest of her three children, Julie, was born. Julie was nine years younger than Ritz's oldest, Joshua, mirroring the age difference between Susan and her own older brother. "I would see Joshua do to Julie what my brother did to me," she says of the taunting and teasing by a much older sibling." I had to try not to always take Julie's side."

While firstborn parent can get into ‘raging battles’ with a firstborn child, youngest parent can help their eldest kids loosen up and not be so hard on themselves, and parents had to try not always take youngest children’s side, which suggests parents' own born order can become an issue when dynamics in the family they are raising replicate the family in which they were raised.

SWT.title: Plug-in Vehicle 电动汽车

blocks.p: Here's a term you're going to hear much more often: plug-in vehicle, and the acronym PEV. It's what you and many other people will drive to work in, ten years and more from now.

At that time, before you drive off in the morning you will first unplug your car - your plug-in vehicle. Its big on-board batteries will have been fully charged overnight, with enough power for you to drive 50-100 kilometers through city traffic.

When you arrive at work you'll plug in your car once again, this time into a socket that allows power to flow from your car's batteries to the electricity grid. One of the things you did when you bought your car was to sign a contract with your favorite electricity supplier, allowing them to draw a limited amount of power from your car's batteries should they need to, perhaps because of a blackout, or very high wholesale spot power prices. The price you get for the power the distributor buys from your car would not only be most attractive to you, it would be a good deal for them too, their alternative being very expensive power form peaking stations.

If, driving home or for some other reason your batteries looked like running flat, a relatively small, but quiet and efficient engine running on petrol, diesel or compressed natural gas, even biofuel, would automatically cut in, driving a generator that supplied the batteries, so you could complete your journey.

Concerns over 'peak oil', increasing greenhouse gas emissions, and the likelihood that by the middle of this century there could be five times as many motor vehicles registered world-wide as there are now, mean that the world's almost total dependence on petroleum-based fuels for transport is, in every sense of the word, unsustainable.

While people can charge their plug-in vehicles overnight before driving, they can plug their vehicles into sockets allowing power to flow from car batteries to the electricity grid, and an engine driving a generator will supply alternative power to complete the journey when the batteries run flat, which means more people will drive plug-in vehicles in the future because the world's almost total dependence on petroleum-based fuels for transport is unsustainable.

SWT.title: Ageing Problem in the World 全球老龄化问题

blocks.p: We live in an ageing world. While this has been recognized for some time in developed countries, it is only recently that this phenomenon has been fully acknowledged. Global communication is "shrinking" the world, and global ageing is "maturing" it. The increasing presence of older persons in the world is making people of all ages more aware that we live in a diverse and multigenerational society. It is no longer possible to ignore ageing, regardless of whether one views it positively or negatively.

Demographers note that if current trends in ageing continue as predicted, a demographic revolution, wherein the proportions of the young and the old will undergo a historic crossover, will be felt in just three generations. This portrait of change in the world's population parallels the magnitude of the industrial revolution traditionally considered the most significant social and economic breakthrough in the history of humankind since the Neolithic period. It marked the beginning of a sustained movement towards modern economic growth in much the same way that globalization is today marking an unprecedented and sustained movement toward a "global culture". The demographic revolution, it is envisaged, will be at least as powerful.

While the future effects are not known, a likely scenario is one where both the challenges as well as the opportunities will emerge from a vessel into which exploration and research, dialogue and debate are poured. Challenges arise as social and economic structures try to adjust to the simultaneous phenomenon of diminishing young cohorts with rising older ones, and opportunities present themselves in the sheer number of older individuals and the vast resources societies stand to gain from their contribution.

While we live in an ageing world, a powerful demographic revolution will be felt in just three generations if current trends continue as predicted, which will bring challenges and opportunities because challenges arise as social and economic structures try to adjust to the simultaneous phenomenon of diminishing young cohorts with rising older ones, and opportunities present themselves in the sheer number of older individuals and the vast resources societies stand to gain from their contribution.
（注：ageing：英式aging：美式；还望摘抄时区分）

SWT.title: Crime Rate 犯罪率

blocks.p: The Home Office’ s periodic British Crime Survey estimates that the true level of crime (the sorts, anyway, which inform the official figures) is about four times that which is registered in the annual statistics.

Quite often, especially in the financial services sector, businesses do not report crimes against themselves for fear of lowering their public image. Many citizens today are not insured against car theft or property loss (because they cannot afford the premiums) so they have no incentive to tell the police if they become victims.

A steep statistical rise in crime can sometimes arise not from a real growth in a particular type of conduct but from a new policing policy - offences of "lewd dancing" rose by about 300 per cent during 12 months in the 1980s in Manchester, but only because the zealous Chief Constable James Anderton had deployed a great many officers in gay night clubs.

Sometimes the enactment of a new range of offences or the possibility of committing old offences in a new way (like computer offences involving fraud and deception) can cause an upward jolt in crime levels. The figures just released show a startling jump in street robbery but much of this seems to be a very particular crime: the theft of the now ubiquitous mobile phones.

Conversely, if crimes like joyriding and some assaults are kept out of the categories measured in the annual statistics, as is the case, the official figures do not reflect even what is reported to the police as criminal.

The way that criminal statistics are compiled by the Home Office is also relevant. From April 1998, police forces started to count crime in a way which, according to the government, will give “a more robust statistical measure".

While business do not report crimes against themselves, a steep statistical rise in crime can sometimes arise from a new policing policy and the enactment of a new range of offences or the possibility of committing old offences in a new way, and the way criminal statistics are compiled by the Home Office is also relevant, which suggests the true level of crime is about four times that which is registered in the annual statistics.

SWT.title: Primary Carers 第一抚养人

blocks.p: Slightly less than one in five carers (19%) were primary carers (475,000 people). That is, they were the main carer of a person who was limited in carrying out the core everyday activities of mobility, communication or self-care. Both primary carers and the larger group of other carers (close to 2 million) contribute to the wellbeing of older people and people with disabilities. However, because they care for people who otherwise would have difficulty carrying out basic everyday activities, there is particular interest in primary carers: in the contribution they make, their wellbeing, labour force experiences, motivations and the support they receive in caring.

Primary carers were more likely than other carers to be assisting someone who lived in the same household (81% compared with 76%). As with caring as a whole, the likelihood of being a primary carer increased with age to peak at age 55-64 years, where one in twenty people were primary carers. However, rather than then declining, the likelihood of being a primary carer remained at around this level among the older age groups. Consequently, primary carers had a somewhat older age profile than other carers. The median age of primary carers was 52 years, compared with 47 years for other carers.

Primary carers were more likely than other carers to be female (71% compared with 50%) and less likely to be in the labour force (39% compared with 60%). Women not in the labour force were by far the largest single group among primary carers (44%). In contrast, men employed full-time were the largest single group among other carers (25%).

While primary carers had a somewhat older age profile, they were more likely to be female, which suggests there is particular interest in them: in the contribution they make, their wellbeing, labour force experiences, motivations and the support they receive in caring, although they were the main carer of a person who was limited in carrying out the core everyday activities of mobility, communication or self-care.

SWT.title: Educational Quality and Equity in Australian 澳州教育的质量和公平性

materials.title: Educational Quality and Equity in Australian
materials.title_zh: 澳州教育的质量和公平性

blocks.p: When Australians engage in debate about educational quality or equity, they often seem to accept that a country cannot achieve both at the same time.

Curriculum reforms intended to improve equity often fail to do so because they increase breadth or differentiation in offerings in a way that increases differences in quality. Further, these differences in quality often reflect differences in students’ social backgrounds because the ‘new’ offerings are typically taken up by relatively disadvantaged students who are not served well them. Evidence from New South Wales will be used to illustrate this point.

The need to improve the quality of education is well accepted across OECD and other countries as they seek to strengthen their human capital to underpin their modern, knowledge economies. Improved equity is also important for this purpose, since the demand for high level skills is widespread and the opportunities for the low skilled are diminishing.

Improved equity in education is also important for social cohesion. There are countries in which the education system seems primarily to reproduce existing social arrangements, conferring privilege where it already exists and denying it where it does not. Even in countries where the diagnosis might be less extreme, the capacity of schooling to build social cohesion is often diminished by the way in which schools separate individuals and groups.

Although the improved quality and equity of education can strengthen human capital to underpin their modern knowledge economies and improve social cohesion, educational quality and equity cannot be both achieved at the same time because curriculum reforms intended to improve equity by increasing breadth or differentiation in offerings also increase differences in quality which reflects differences in students’ social backgrounds.

SWT.title: Academic Networking 学术届人际网络

blocks.p: Getting to know fellow academics, especially more senior ones, can be very daunting. Lecturers and researchers are used to spending a lot of time in isolation working independently. The thought of going public and ‘selling yourself' does not seem enticing. However, it is easier than you think to begin to develop your own career-enhancing networks. Your PhD supervisor and examiners or if you are already in post, your mentor, are a great place to start. They will have been chosen to guide you because they are more experienced and in most cases they will work close to your field of interest. Ask their advice for ways of building up your own network of contacts. Also it is easier to approach someone unknown to you if you can mention the name of a mutual acquaintance.

If you are a postgraduate who is serious about a career in academia, or a more senior scholar wanting to develop one, you will surely be attending conferences on a fairly regular basis. There is no right or wrong number of these, some scholars stick to one or two a year, others seem to attend one a month! Conferences are the main way that academics network with each other, so do not miss out on these opportunities. If you are presenting a paper it gives others a chance to see what you are working on, and the informal sections of the programme (such as food and drink breaks) encourage mingling and further discussion.

Although getting to know fellow academics can be very daunting and not enticing because lecturers and researchers spend a lot of time in isolation working independently, it is easier to begin to develop your own career-enhancing networks by starting with your supervisor and examiners or your mentor because they are more experienced and know more people, and by attending conferences because they are the main way that academics network with each other.

SWT.title: Ageing Australia 澳大利亚老龄化问题

blocks.p: In 2005 Japan had the highest median age of all countries in the world, while Australia's population was only moderately aged. Some 50 years ago the demographic situation was quite different, with the median age of Australia's population being seven years older than Japan's. The ageing of the population is a major issue for Australian policy makers, particularly in regard to the long-term implications for reduced economic growth and the increasing demand for Age Pensions, and health and aged care services. As the population ages, growth in the number of people of working age will slow, while the proportion of people of retirement age will increase.

Sustained population ageing also leads to slowing or negative population growth. While declining population growth in developed countries is welcomed by some environmentalist and social scientists, economists tend to agree that population decline brings gloomy economic prospects. In addition to the decrease in the labor supply, the demand side of the economy may be affected through shrinking markets for goods and services.

How quickly this occurs depends on the dynamics of fertility, mortality and overseas migration. While a moderate pace of demographic change allows for gradual adjustment of the economy and policies to the changing population demographics, rapid changes are more difficult to manage. As a result, governments and society as a whole may need to take actions to address these issues.

Although Australia’s population was moderately aged, the aging of the population is still a major issue for Australian policy makers because it not only has long-term implications for reduced economic growth and the increasing demand for Age Pensions, but also leads to slowing or negative population growth, and how quickly this occurs depends on the dynamics of fertility, mortality and migration, which suggests governments and society need to take actions to address these issues together.

SWT.title: Girls Educational Degree

blocks.p: If women are so far ahead of men, why are they so far behind? Reports from both sides of the Atlantic show that female students dominate university courses, yet women still do not make it to the top. A report on inequality in the UK said last week that girls had better educational results than boys at 16, went to university in greater numbers and achieved better degrees once they got there. “More women now have higher education qualifications than men in every age group up to age 44,” the report said. In the US, 57 per cent of college graduates in 2006-07 were women. Women form the majority of all graduates under 45.

Yet few women make it to the boards of companies in either country. In the UK, the proportion of women on FTSE 100 boards rose fractionally from 11.7 per cent to 12.2 per cent last year, according to the Cranfield University School of Management, but that was only because of a fall in the size of the boards. In the US, women accounted for 15.2 per cent of board seats on Fortune 500 companies, according to Catalyst, the research organisation, which said the numbers had barely budged for five years. The hopeful way of looking at this is that the rising generation of female graduates has yet to reach director age. Give it 10 years and they will dominate boards as they do universities. If that were true, however, we would surely see the number of women director numbers moving up by now. The first year that women college graduates outnumbered men in the US was 1982. These graduates must be entering their 50s – prime director age.

Although female students dominate university course, women still do not make it to the top and few women make it to the boards of companies in either country, and the hopeful way of looking at this is that the rising generation of female graduates has yet to reach director age, but we haven't see the number of women director numbers moving up by now, which suggests women are so far behind.

SWT.title: Overqualified Employees 能力过好的员工

blocks.p: If your recruiting efforts attract job applicants with too much experience—a near certainty in this weak labor market—you should consider a response that runs counter to most hiring managers’ MO: Don’t reject those applicants out of hand. Instead, take a closer look. New research shows that overqualified workers tend to perform better than other employees, and they don’t quit any sooner. Furthermore, a simple managerial tactic—empowerment—can mitigate any dissatisfaction they may feel.

The prejudice against too-good employees is pervasive. Companies tend to prefer an applicant who is a “perfect fit” over someone who brings more intelligence, education, or experience than needed. On the surface, this bias makes sense: Studies have consistently shown that employees who consider themselves overqualified exhibit higher levels of discontent. For example, over- qualification correlated well with job dissatisfaction in a 2008 study of 156 call-center reps by Israeli researchers Saul Fine and Baruch Nevo. And unlike discrimination based on age or gender, declining to hire overqualified workers is perfectly legal.

But even before the economic downturn, a surplus of overqualified candidates was a global problem, particularly in developing economies, where rising education levels are giving workers more skills than are needed to supply the growing service sectors. If managers can get beyond the conventional wisdom, the growing pool of too-good applicants is a great opportunity. Berrin Erdogan and Talya N. Bauer of Portland State University in Oregon found that overqualified workers’ feelings of dissatisfaction can be dissipated by giving them autonomy in decision making. At stores where employees didn’t feel empowered, “overeducated” workers expressed greater dissatisfaction than their colleagues did and were more likely to state an intention to quit. But that difference vanished where self-reported autonomy was high.

Although prejudice against too-good employees is pervasive and companies tend to prefer an application who is perfect-fit because employees who consider themselves overqualified exhibit higher levels of discontent, a surplus of overqualified candidates was a global problem, but new research shows that overqualified workers not only tend to perform better than other employees but also don’t quit any sooner, and a simple managerial tactic, empowerment, can mitigate any dissatisfaction they may feel.

SWT.title: Library Development and Social Media 图书馆发展与社交媒体

materials.title: Library Development and Social Media
materials.title_zh: 图书馆发展与社交媒体

blocks.p: Ten years ago, Barsky and Purdon (20SWT：06) discovered that social networks that are expanding communication through social media are becoming popular and the costs involved are getting further reduced. Yet, library executives did not see how such a phenomenon could become a part of library and information services. They felt that the users should be left to their social media while the library carried on with its traditional roles (De Rosa et al.,2007).

This was also the case when Charnigo and Barnett-Ellis (2007) conducted a survey of 126 academic librarians and concluded that 54% of the librarians surveyed did not believe that there was an academic purpose for Facebook. The rationale behind these librarians’ belief was that social media was a space where students interact with each other. Hence, the librarian was not welcome as their coming in might be viewed as an invasion of space.

But time has proved that as the technology of social media became more popular, users and librarians acquired digital literacy, and libraries, seeing an explosion of social media around it, were forced to reconsider their stance. In a survey involving 497 international librarians, Taylor & Francis (2014) discovered that over 70% of librarians now feel that the use of social media is important. Though the wave began with public libraries (Mon, 2015), today, libraries of every type either have a social media presence or they are seriously considering it. Hence, the use of social media by libraries has become mainstream.

Although social networks that are expanding communication, library executives did not see social media could become a part of library and information services and it was not welcome because social media was a space where students interact with each other, but the use of social media by libraries has become mainstream because as the technology of social media became more popular, users and librarians acquired digital literacy, and libraries were forced to reconsider their stance.

RO.title: Ada Lovelace 埃达·洛夫莱斯

list: Ada Lovelace has been the subject of some biographies, some scholarly, some popular.
From these, we learn that Augusta Ada King, Countess of Lovelace, was a nineteenth-century aristocrat whose initial claim to fame was simply the fact that she was the daughter of the poet Lord Byron.
From her birth, society at large speculated about whether the young Ada would grow up to be like her father.

Indeed, one of the enduring myths about Lovelace is that her mother, Lady Byron, deliberately steered Ada’s studies towards mathematics and science in order to dampen any ‘poetical’ tendencies that she may have inherited from her father.

The truth, however, is rather more prosaic: Lady Byron had herself been educated in mathematics, unusually for a woman at this time, and had enjoyed it — it seems that she simply wanted the same opportunities for her daughter.

RO.title: The Candle and Its Flame 蜡烛与火焰

list: When a candle burns, the flame heats the nearby air and starts to rise.
As this warm air moves up, cooler air and oxygen rush in at the bottom of the flame to replace it.
When that cooler air is heated, it too rises up and is replaced by cooler air at the base of the flame.
This creates a continual cycle of upward moving air around the flame (a convection current), which gives the flame its elongated or teardrop shape.

list: During the school year, we had the benefit of being both unaccountable and omnipotent.

Fernando 的研究最后导致了对整个神经生物学领域已有知识的彻底检查。
Animal behavior is a fast changing field and there are lots of new developments.

blocks.p: Why should we bother studying animal behavior? Well, first and foremost, because we are interested in understanding why animals do what they do. There are lots of other reasons for studying animal behavior. Conservation biologists need to know what animals do if they're going to save them. Are those animals social or solitary? How much space do they need and how many mates do they have? Sometimes you can’t predict the outcome of the research. Fernando Nottebohm started out being interested in how birds know what to sing. Yet his research eventually led to a complete overhaul of the entire field of neurobiology, a totally unanticipated yet utterly monumental effect. And this is the course textbook by John Alcock. The fact that this is in its ninth edition tells you how fast a field animal behaviour is. There are lots of new developments.

People usually think of robots as cute, cuddly toys as Hollywood depictions.
人们通常认为机器人是可爱的玩具，就像好莱坞描述的那样。
The first robots were created and imagined in the time of political turmoil after First World War.
最早的机器人是在第一次世界大战之后直接政局动荡中产生和想象出来的。
People reflected on what does it mean to be a human.

blocks.p: This is a kind of object that you're probably all familiar with. When you had the term robot, but I'm gonna show you the very, very first robots. These were the very first robots. They were characters in a play in the 1920s called Rossum's Universal Robots, and they…, the play was written by Czech writer called Karel Capek. And basically, these robots, you know, people tend to think of robots as kind of cute cuddly toys or, you know, Hollywood depictions kind of devoid of politics. But the first robots were actually created and imagined in a time of absolute political turmoil. You just had the First World War, you know, it finished and had a devastating impact across Europe and so people will kind… and people are kind of reflecting on “What does it mean to be human”, “what makes us human”

those kinds of question. And this kind of context is what inspired Capek to kind of write this play. And interestingly, these robots being human, they are actually in the play assembled on a production line, a bit like the Ford manufacturing production line. So even though they are human, they are assembled and these robots are designed to labour, and that is their primary purpose in society.

威尔逊来自一个不同的世界( 意指他与其他人的观点不同)，他是每美国大众主流文化的焦点。
He wanted modern literature to be able to be read and appreciated by ordinary people
他希望现代文学能够成为普通人都能阅读和欣赏的文学。
He was also successful in equalling the great cultures of Europe in American life.
他同时成功地使欧洲文化与美国文化等同起来（不分孰优孰劣）。
He believed that literature was as much of a part of life for everyone as conversation.
他认为文学就如同日常谈话那样，是生活的重要组成部分。
Wilson was also a very various man.
威尔逊他也是一个有着多重身份（指头衔）的人。

blocks.p: Wilson came from a different world. And he became the focal point of a broad mainstream American culture that thought that modern literature and wanted modern literature to be able to be read and appreciated by ordinary people. They were not modernists in an abstract sense. And certainly, some of them like TS Eliot and Faulkner were too difficult for some of their writings to be read by ordinary people. But this was a world before the division between the brows or between a lead or whatever had established itself as a part of our consciousness.
Wilson was a major player in the successful effort of his generation to establish at the heart of American life and innovative literature
that would equal the great cultures of Europe. And he knew that the great cultures of Europe were there. He was not a product of a narrow American Studies kind of training at all.

He joined a high artistic standard with an openness to all experience and a belief that literature was as much of a part of life for everyone as conversation. He thought the Proust and Joyce and Yeats and Eliot could and should be read by ordinary Americans and helped that to happen.

蜜蜂跳摇摆舞来引导其他蜜蜂去采集花蜜。
But researchers have found that dancing can be halted by a head butt from another bee as a warning signal.
但是研究者发现，如果一只蜜蜂用头撞击另一只作为危险信号，他们就会停止跳舞。
They set up a lab mimicking a source of a nectar and foraging bees were introduced to the dangers of competition from rival colonies.
研究者在实验室模拟一个花蜜源，然后将蜜蜂引入争夺地盘的危险中。
Their behaviour of stopping bee’s dancing is warns of a dangerous source of nectar.
蜜蜂会停止跳舞，这是其实是他们发出的危险信号。

blocks.p: Honey bees do a waggle dance to direct other bees to sources of nectar (花蜜). But dancing bees like this one can be halted by a head butt from another bee. Now researches have found that this head butt is actually a warning signal. A feeding station was set up in the lab to mimic a source of nectar. Then foraging bees were introduced to the dangers at the station such as competition from rival colonies. When foragers returned to the hive, they stopped bee’s dancing. Scientist think the behavior warns dancers of a dangerous source of nectar.

RL.title: Linguists and Linguistic Authorities 语言学家与语言权

blocks.p: 配图：图中有部分录音内容

pairs: When we move into working with communities, we have to recognize that the communities have to be the authority in their language.
当我们开始与社区合作时，我们得承认社区对它们自己的语言拥有权威。
There is a distinction between expertise and authority.
专业知识和权威是不同的。
Linguists have expertise in certain very narrow areas of language, but we don't have the authority of the language the community produces.
语言学家在某个特殊的、比较狭窄的领域拥有专业知识，但是我们并不拥有该社区说的语言的权威。
The bottom line is languages are lost because of the dominance of one people over another.
结果是如果一个人的影响力超过了另一个人，语言就会灭绝。
In working with language revival, if we continue to hold the authority, so in a sense, the languages are still lost if the authority is still lost.
在语言复兴中，如果我们（指语言学家）仍然拥有权威，在某种程度上，如果权威没有放对，语言仍然会消失。

blocks.p: But when we move into working with communities, we have to recognize that the communities have to be the authority in their language. Actually, a woman in the class I'm teaching at Sydney at the moment, a career woman, expressed this very nicely, although she was talking about something else. She was distinguishing expertise from authority. And certainly linguists because of our training we do have expertise in certain very narrow areas of language, but we don't have the authority over what to do with that knowledge or what to do with other knowledge that the community produces. I guess for me the bottom line is languages are lost because of the dominance of one people over another. That's not rocket science. It's not hard to work that out. But then what that means is if in working with language revival we continue to hold the authority, we actually haven't done anything towards undoing how languages are lost in the first place, so in a sense, the languages are still lost if the authority is still lost.

RL.title: Green Revolution and Rice 绿色革命和大米

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The Green Revolution began in 1943 when Mexico was unable to feed its growing population and sought for help.
绿色革命始于1943 年，因为那时墨西哥没有足够粮食，在寻求帮助。
The International Rice Research Institute was founded in Asia.
随后，世界大米研究所在亚洲成立。
By 1962, a new strain of rice called IR8 was the first modified crop, producing five times the yield of traditional rice varieties.
到 1962 年，一种叫 IR8 的新型大米是第一种转基因水稻，产量是传统水稻的5 倍。
By 1980, IR36 resisted pests and grew fast enough to allow two crops a year instead of just one, doubling the yield.
到 1980 年，IR36 型水稻可以防止害虫，一年可收获两次，产量是IR8 型的2 倍。
By 1990, using more advanced genetic manipulation techniques, IR72 was outperforming even IR36.
到1990 年，科学家使用了更先进的基因操控技术，IR72 型大米的表现超过了IR36 型。
The Green Revolution saw worldwide crop yields explode from 1960 through 2000.
从1960 年到2000 年，绿色革命见证了全球大米产量爆发式的增长。

blocks.p: In 1943, what became known as the Green Revolution began when Mexico, unable to feed its growing population, shouted for help. Within a few years, the Ford and Rockefeller Foundations founded the International Rice Research Institute in Asia, and by 1962, a new strain of rice called IR8 was feeding people all over the world. IR8 was the first really big modified crop to make a real impact on world hunger. In 1962 the technology did not yet exist to directly manipulate the genes of plants, and so IR8 was created by carefully crossing existing varieties: selecting the best from each generation, further modifying them, and finally finding the best. Here is the power of modified crops: IR8, with no fertilizer, straight out of the box, produced five times the yield of traditional rice varieties. In optimal conditions with nitrogen, it produced ten times the yield of traditional varieties. By 1980, IR36
resisted
pests
and

grew fast enough to allow two crops a year instead of just one, doubling the yield. And by 1990, using more advanced genetic manipulation techniques, IR72 was outperforming even IR36. The Green Revolution saw worldwide crop yields explode from 1960 through 2000.

RL.title: Superhuman Strength during a Crisis 危机时刻的超能力

blocks.p: 配图：如上，近似图

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: There are heroic tales of superhuman feats, such as some people having incredible power to lift a car or move giant rocks in the face of a disaster.
有很多关于超能力的英雄故事，比如说某个人在灾难中抬起车子或者推动石头。
In proper terminology, such a temporary boost of physical power would be called hysterical strength.
力气短暂暴增，术语叫做“hysterica l strength”。
The majority of them are anecdotal, and interestingly not repeatable.
这些现象的大多属于奇闻逸事，并且没有办法重复。
Basically, these anecdotes suggest that in times of crisis, danger, or fear, some people have the ability to temporarily exercise superhuman strength.
这些奇闻逸事说明，人们在面对危机、危险或者恐惧的时候，有能力暂时拥有超越人类极限的力量。

blocks.p: Today we're going to recount heroic tales of superhuman feats of strength, when in the face of disaster, some people are said to have summoned up incredible physical power to lift a car off of an accident victim, move giant rocks, or like Big John of song, single-handedly hold up a collapsing beam to let the other miners escape. Are such stories true? There are many anecdotes supporting the idea, but we're going to take a fact-based look at whether or not it truly is possible for an adrenalin-charged person to temporarily gain massive strength. In proper terminology, such a temporary boost of physical power would be called hysterical strength. The stories are almost always in the form of one person lifting a car off of another. And even lifting many cars by several inches still leaves most of its weight supported by the suspension springs. But our purpose today is not to "debunk" any of the specific stories. The majority of them are anecdotal, and interestingly not repeatable; in many cases, the person who summoned the super strength later tried it again only to find that they couldn't do it. Basically,
what we have is a respectably large body of anecdotal evidence that suggests that in times of crisis, danger, or fear, some people have the ability to temporarily exercise superhuman strength.

RL.title: Survey 调查

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: A survey shows that 62% of the people reply on internet to obtain news, while others say they reply on newspaper, TV and radio.
一项调查显示，62%的人群依赖互联网读新闻，而其他人说他们从报纸、电视和电台获取新闻。
But actually, this survey is conducted on the website globalandmail.com.
但事实上，这个调查是由一个叫 global and mail.com 的网站进行的。
The people who did this survey on a website must be frequent users of internet.
参与调查的人肯定是互联网常用用户。
This sample is a biased sample. So we have to pay attention to how a survey is conducted.
这个样本是带有偏见的样本，所以特别注意一个调查是如何进行的。

blocks.p: Let's say if I'm asking which source do you often use to get information. Newspaper? Radio? TV? And the survey shows 62% of the people chose internet. You might be thinking I am going to say, how important the internet is, or how quickly it has changed the world for a few years. But what if I tell you this survey is conducted on the website globalandmail.com? Our answer will be different because the people who did this survey on a website must be frequent users of internet. This sample is a biased sample. So we have to pay attention to how a survey is conducted.

RL.title: Open Borders 开放边境

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Developed countries should open borders to people from other countries as it is to everyone’s interest.
发达国家应该对其他国家的人开放边境，因为这符合所有人的利益。
As a principle, opening orders reduces injustice and allow freedom.
从原则的角度，开放边境可以减少不公正，促进自由。
In terms of humanity, it helps people from poorer countries.
从人道主义来说，这可以帮助贫穷国家的人民。
Economically, opening borders makes developed countries richer.
从经济上来说，开放边境可以使得发达国家更加富裕。
In pragmatic terms, opening borders is inevitable.
从现实角度来看，开放边境势在必行。

blocks.p: I believe our borders should be open. But if that is not politically acceptable for now, Europe should at least open up a legal route for people from developing countries to come work here. Over time, hopefully, we can move to a position where borders are completely open. Persuading sceptics won't be easy. That’s why I think the argument for free migration has to be made at several levels. A principled case, it increases freedom and reduces injustice. A humanitarian case, it helps people much poorer than ourselves. An economic case, it makes us richer. And a pragmatic case, it is inevitable, so it is in everyone’s interests to make the best of it. Freedom of movement is not just a matter of human rights and international solidarity（团结一致）. It is in our self-interest. Opening our borders may seem unrealistic. But so too, once did abolishing slavery or giving women the vote. Campaigning for people’s right to vote freely is a noble cause for our time.
配PPT：上面列出了4 个要点（case）

RL.title: Cracking Knee 膝盖粉碎

blocks.p: 配图：如上
注：本音频还考过听力的单选题

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Omer Inan, an electrical engineer at Georgia Tech, think there's some real information in the sound of a cracking knee.
Gerogia Tech 的电子工程师Omer Inan 认为膝盖粉碎的声音里藏着某种有用的信息。
The sound can be exploited for the purposes of helping people with rehabilitation.
研究这种声音，可以帮助有膝盖粉碎的人康复。
He and a team of physiologists and engineers built a prototype with stretchy athletic tape and a few tiny mics and skin sensors.
他和一群理疗学家和工程师一起发明了一种装有小型麦克风和皮肤传感器的可伸缩运动胶带。
It might allow patients and doctors to track healing after surgery.
这个胶带可以让病人和医生追踪术后的康复情况。
The primary application we're targeting at first is to give people a decision aid about different intensities of particular activities during rehabilitation.
它最主要的应用是能够帮助病人在康复过程中决定做哪种强度的运动。

blocks.p: 参考答案：

The sound of a cracking knee isn't particularly pleasant. But it gets worse when you listen up close. "It does for most people. But for me, it just makes me excited." Omer Inan, an electrical engineer at Georgia Tech. "I actually feel like there's some real information in them that can be exploited for the purposes of helping people with rehab."
Inan's experience with cracking knees goes back to his days as an undergrad at Stanford, where he threw discus（铁饼）. "If I had a
really hard workout, then the next day of course I'd be sore, but I'd also sometimes feel this basically catching or popping or creaking every now and then in my knee."

A few years later, he found himself building tiny microphones at a high-end audio company. So when he got to Georgia Tech and heard the Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency, DARPA, wanted better tech for knee injuries, he thought: Why not strap tiny microphones to people's knees, to eavesdrop（偷听，窃听）as their legs bend?" What we think it is, is the cartilage （软骨）and bone rubbing against each other, the surfaces inside the knee rubbing against each other, during those movements."

He and a team of physiologists and engineers built a prototype with stretchy athletic tape and a few tiny mics and skin sensors. And preliminary tests on athletes suggest the squishy sounds the device picks up are more erratic（不稳定的）, and more irregular, in an injured knee than in a healthy one, which Inan says might allow patients and doctors to track healing after surgery. Details appear in the IEEE Transactions on Biomedical Engineering.

"The primary application we're targeting at first is to give people a decision aid during rehabilitation, following an acute knee injury, to help them understand when they can perform particular activities, and when they can move to different intensities of particular activities." A useful thing to take a crack at.

RL.title: Gross National Happiness 全民幸福指数

夹在中国和印度之间的小国不丹，是唯一一个以全民幸福指数为核心来考量政府政策的国家。
It has achieved a good deal of success in education, health, economic growth and environmental preservation.
它在教育、医疗、经济和环保上都取得了巨大成功。
Other countries are now interested in happiness research and would like to use it more for public policy.
其他国家也对幸福研究产生兴趣，想要将其应用于公共政策的制定中。
It is beginning to become a subject of greater interest for policymakers and legislators in different advanced countries such as Australia, France and Great Britain.
在澳洲、法国和英国等发达国家中，幸福指数已变成了政策制定者和立法者的重要关注点。

blocks.p: Only one country, tiny little Bhutan, wedged between China and India, has adopted the Gross National Happiness as the central index of government policy, and actually has a good deal of success in education and in health and in economic growth and in environmental preservation. And They have a rather sophisticated way of measuring the effects of different policies on people’s happiness. But they are the only country to go that far. But you are now beginning to get other countries interested enough to do kind of white paper policy analyses about happiness research – what effects would it have if we used it more for public policy? You are beginning to get countries like Australia, France, Great Britain, that are considering publishing regular statistics on happiness. So it is beginning to become a subject of greater interest for policymakers and legislators in different advanced countries.

非营利机构行业价值 1 万亿，在澳大利亚，有70 万个这样的组织。
The UN recognized 37,000 civil society groups and gave 3,500 accreditations.
联合国承认了3 万7 千个民间社会团体，并认证了其中的3 千500 个。

blocks.p: But in the face of this sense of disempowerment, there surprisingly is no decline in involvement in organizations which seek to share wealth and opportunities, protect one another’s rights and work towards the common good. According to the United Nations, civil society groups have grown 40 folds since the turn of last century.
配PPT：PPT 上有文字和数据，可以照读

Internationally, the non-profit sector is worth one trillion dollars, and there are 700,000 such organizations in Australia alone. The UN recognizes 37,000 specifically civil society organizations across the globe, and gave 3,500 accreditations to the 2002 World Summit on Sustainable Development. This profound movement towards harnessing voices and resources from outside the realm of governments and officialdom reflects a profound growth in NGOS, "the third sector, as some call it. As Robert Putnam discovered in the field of local government in Italy the best predictor of governmental success was the strength and density of a region's civic associations.

The end product for me was always better understanding or when one really succeeded in unifying theory that can help us in teaching the subject.
研究的最终产物是对教书有更好的理解，或者当人把理论和实践相结合的时候，帮我们把书教好。
I've also looked at teaching as a vehicle to try new ideas, or new ways to doing things on an intelligent group of learners
通过教育，我可以尝试新想法，或在一群智力超群的学习者身上用新方法教书。
And in my experience, this kind of teaching is the most stimulated and motivating to students.
根据我的经验，这种教书方式才是最激励学生的。
It is this unity and close connection of research and teaching recognized the successful professor.
这是研究和实际教学的统一和密切关联，使得一个人成为一个成功的教授。

blocks.p: All my research and that I conducted was my 60 plus graduate students, was motivated by their need to learn, so that we can teach. Of course, in some inventions happened along the way but I've always considered the end result. And I always consider that this invention to be by-product, by-products of the learning process. The end product for me was always better understanding or when one really succeeded in unifying theory that can help us in teaching the subject. I've also looked at teaching as a vehicle to try new ideas, or new ways to doing things on an intelligent group of learners. That is as the vehicle for the teaching research results. And in my experience, this kind of teaching is the most stimulated and motivating to students. I am also uncovered many interesting research problems is the cause of teaching the subject. It is this unity of research and teaching their close connection and the benefits gathered by exercising and the interplay that to be recognized the successful professor.

RL.title: Bomb Calorimeter 弹式热量计

blocks.p: 配图：上图仅为近似图片，非原图

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Bomb calorimeter can measure how much energy is contained in food.
弹式热量计可以测量食物的热量。
The combustion of food with oxygen happened in cylinder in the device and the water chamber absorbs the heat when food samples are burned.
食物与氧气混合，在气缸中燃烧。充水的弹膛可以吸收食物燃烧的热量。
However, the energy measured by the calorimeter is different from the digestible energy in human body because our digestion system cannot absorb all energy from food.
但是，用这种热量计测出的热量和人体可消化的热量是不同的，因为我们的消化系统并不能吸收食物中所有的热量。

RL.title: Economic Structure in Europe 欧洲经济结构的改变

blocks.p: 配图：黑白图片，是一张欧洲的建筑图，图没有用

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: After the Industrial Revolution, the economic structure in Europe change dramatically around the beginning of 19th century.
工业革命之后，在19 世纪初前后，欧洲的经济结构发生了巨大变化。
Since lots of machinery such as steam engine had been used in manufacturing, the circulation for goods and services increased significantly.
因为大量像蒸汽机这样的的机器在生产中投入使用，商品和服务的流通速度大幅加快。
Consequently, it leads to an expansion of middle class population and accumulation of social wealth.
这使得中产阶级人口增多，并累计了大量的财富。

RL.title: Civilization 文明

blocks.p: 配图：如上，有码头和集装箱

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Civilization is like a huge ship, sailing to the future faster and faster than we have expected.
人类文明好比一艘巨大的船，比我们预想速度更快更远地驶向未来。
We cannot foresee the future, but we could study the safety records of the ship and the capabilities of its crew.
我们不能预知未来，但是我们可以研究这艘船的安全航行记录和船员的能力。
Our ship is not only the largest, but also the last one.
我们的这艘船不仅是最大的，也是最后一艘。
Intelligence has made the world smaller.
人类智力使得世界变得更小。
As we have push forward so far, it is imperative that we protect the environment.
我们已经在这条路上走得太远，保护环境刻不容缓。
We cannot afford to progress by trial and error any more.
我们不能再通过试错来获得进步了。

RL.title: High LG and Low LG Rats 老鼠的舔舐和理毛实验

materials.title: High LG and Low LG Rats
materials.title_zh: 老鼠的舔舐和理毛实验

blocks.p: 配图：如上

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Differences in stress reactivity of adult rats are determined by maternal licking and grooming during infancy.
成年老鼠在压力反应中的不同是由母鼠对幼鼠的舔舐和理毛决定的。
L means licking and G means grooming.
L 指舔舐，G 指理毛。
Some mother rats spend a lot of time licking, grooming and nursing their pups, while others seem to ignore their pups.
一些母鼠会花很多时间照顾幼鼠，舔舐他们和为他们理毛，但其他母鼠并不这样。
High LG lead to modest stress reactivity and reduced risk for poor development and disease.
高 LG 的成年老鼠有适度的压力反应，有更好的发展和更低的疾病发病率。
Low LG lead to increased stress reactivity and increase risk for heart disease, diabetes and other diseases
低LG 的成年老鼠压力反应会增大，且心脏病、糖尿病等疾病的发病率会更大。

“固定薪资”只支付销售人员固定的薪酬，这不能很好地激励高级销售人员。
The “commission only” plan pays in direct proportion to sales.
“佣金”方案只支付销售业绩的固定比例给销售人员。

The third way is the combination between the two, which is salary plus commission, and it is the best way to motivate salespeople.

RL.title: Language Disorder 语言障碍

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Language disorder is children ’ s disability to produce speech.
语言障碍指儿童无法说话。
In UK/US, 10% of the population suffer from it, we need to address the problem.
在英国/美国，10%的儿童有语言障碍，因此我们要解决这个问题。
We need to know what language is and how it can be learnt.
我们要知道语言是什么，以及它是怎样被习得的。
Language disorder in children is different from that is in adults, so it should be dealt with separately.
儿童的语言障碍不同于成人，所以应该分开对待。
Not being able to generate sentences in children is a psychological question, while in adults it is a logical question.
儿童无法说出完整的句子是一个心理问题（此处不确定），而成人则是一个逻辑问题（意思是他们没有逻辑，所以说不出话）。

RL.title: Soot Emission 煤烟排放

blocks.p: 配图：如上

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Soot is also known as black carbon. It is released when you burn down coal, diesel fuel and wood.
烟尘也叫黑炭。当你烧煤炭、柴油和木头的时候就会释放烟尘。
Soot contributes to global warming, but does not accumulate in the atmosphere like CO2.
全球变暖跟烟尘排放相关，但是烟尘不像二氧化碳一样会在空气中积累。
Reduction in soot have immediate but not long-term effects on global warming.
减少空气中的烟尘能够对全球变暖产生即时效果，但无法有长期的效果。
So if we want to stabilize the climate system, we need to focus on greenhouse gases such as CO2.
所以如果我们想要使得气候稳定的话，我们必须关注如二氧化碳这样的温室气体。

RL.title: Community Service Workers in India 印度的社工

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Health trainings are essential for community service workers in India where HIV is difficult to control.
印度的 HIV 传播很难控制。对印度社工的健康培训很重要。
Trainings and consultations help them to understand knowledge of precaution and prevent disease from spreading.
培训和咨询有助于社工了解防范知识，获知如何防止疾病传播。
They will be provided by big hospitals and professionals.
这些培训和咨询由大医院和专家提供。
However, large workshops and seminars are not necessary in some areas as the target groups are hard to reach.
但是，在一些地区，因为很难找到目标人群，没有必要举办大型的研讨会和研讨班 。

RL.title: Mega Cities 超大城市

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The development mega cities bring huge impact.
超大城市的发展带来了许多负面影响。
In 1990, the population was about 1.5 billion, but it increased 4 folds to 6 billion in 2000.
从 1990 年到 2000 年，城市人口从15 亿增长到60 忆，翻了4 倍。
Meanwhile, resource consumption increased by 16 folds over the century.
同时，能源的消耗也增长了 16 倍。
Due to globalization and urbanization, cities only take up 2% of the land, but have 50% of the population and consume 75% of the resources.
由于全球化和城市化进程，虽然城市只占用了2%的土地，却容纳着 50%的人口，消耗着 75% 的资源。
Not only that, people also produce tons of wastes.
不仅如此，城市人口还制造了大量的垃圾。

RL.title: 041. Three Stages of Brain Development 大脑发育的三个阶段

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Human brain development is a development process of language and cognition.
人类大脑发育是一个语言和认知发展的过程。
The three stages are primitive brain, limbic brain and neocortex.
其发展的三个时期分别为原脑、脑边缘系统和大脑皮质。
Different sections of the brain have different functions and finished development in different times.
大脑不同的部位负责不同的功能，也在不同的时期停止发展。
Sensory pathways, including vision and hearing, develop from embryo (['embrɪəʊ]) time, peak at 3 months old and stop at more than 4 year olds.
感觉传导路径包括视觉和听觉，从胚胎时期发育，3 个月时达到顶峰，到4 岁停止发育。
Language develops from embryo time, peaks around 9 months, and stops around 4 years old.
语言也从胚胎时期开始发育，9 个月时达到顶峰，4 岁左右停止发展。
Higher cognitive function starts the earliest, peaks around 1 year old, and stops before 16.
高等认知功能发展得最早，在1 岁时达到峰值，16 岁前停止发育。

RL.title: Pavlov’s Experiment of Conditioning Ver. 2 巴普洛夫实验版本二

blocks.p: 配图：如上

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The experiment explains how motivation works and how dog’s brain works as well as human’s.
这个实验解释了动机的原理，以及狗和人类的大脑如何工作。
First, when the bell rings, it serves as a cue for the dog.
首先，当铃响的时候，它对于狗来说是一种信号。
Based on the cue, the dog’s will have a certain anticipation.
基于这个信号，狗的大脑会产生一定的预期。
Then, if food comes, the outcome meets the anticipation, and dog will be happy.
之后，如果食物来了，这个结果就与预期相同，呢么狗就会开心。
It is conducted by Pavlov a century ago and classic conditioning.
巴浦洛夫一百多年前就做了这个实验，被称作经典条件反射。

RL.title: Narratives 叙述

blocks.p: 配图：黑白卡通图片，异常花里胡哨，像是在一个工厂里

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: We sometimes use different kinds of methods to describe a situation.
我们会用不同的方法来描述一个场景。
Sometimes we have to use dynamics of visualization, particularly when we do not witness the scenario and have narratives of others.
有时我们需要利用动态的可视化的方法来做描述，尤其一件事我们没有亲眼所见，而来自他人的描述。
The speaker often asks his mother about the Second World War, asking where a family came from, what the shelter looked like and when did she live there.
讲话人经常问他母亲关于二战的问题，某个家族来自哪里，帐篷长什么样子以及她何时住的帐篷。
From her narratives, the speaker can obtain more evidence for his book.
通过母亲的描述，讲话人可以为自己写书积累证据和素材。

blocks.p: The comics I show you with lots of people chatting around in a room is a form of description. We use different kinds of methods to describe a situation. Sometimes we have to use visual description, particularly when we do not witness the scenario. I was born during the Second World War and my hometown is X, for example when I asked my mother about the war, I always ask her you have mentioned this or that when you talked to me when asked her about the shelter, I asked her what the shelter looks like and when did you go to the shelter. From her response I could get more visual evidence as I can to write my book.

RL.title: Determinants of Human behavior 人类行为的决定因素

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Human behavior is determined by two factors: internal and external factors.
人类行为由两个因素决定，内在因素和外在因素。
Internal factors are also personal factors, including one ’ s thoughts, beliefs, and ideas.
内在因素即个人因素，包括一个人的思想、信仰和观点。
External factors are environmental factors, such as weather, temperature and the people around them.
外在因素即环境因素，比如天气、温度和周围的人。
Therefore, human ’ s behavior is determined by himself and environment.
因此，人的行为是由自己和环境决定的。

RL.title: Children Obesity 儿童肥胖症

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Children obesity and overweight problems are a major concern of parents and the society.
儿童肥胖症和超重问题是家长和社会共同关注的问题。
About 20% of total children population are obese.
20%的儿童有不同程度的肥胖。
Heart diseases happened to adults aged 50 to 60 years old in the past, but the youngest who got heart diseases is 5 years old.
以前五六十岁的成人才会得心脏病，但是现在得心脏病最小的只有5 岁。
Obesity makes heart attack and other health problems such as blindness happen earlier and earlier.
肥胖使得心脏和失明等健康问题的发病年龄越来越早
Obesity can cause many negative health consequences, including type 2 diabetes, kidney failure, and stroke.
肥胖会导致很多健康问题，比如 2 型糖尿病、肾衰竭和中风。

RL.title: British Press and Freedom of Speech 英国媒体与英国言论自由

materials.title: British Press and Freedom of Speech
materials.title_zh: 英国媒体与英国言论自由

blocks.p: 配图：略像油画的一幅图

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The British press came into being in the 18th century.
英国的媒体产生于18 世纪。
Freedom of speech were encouraged since then.
从那时开始，政府就鼓励言论自由。
People could talk about anything in public places such as in coffee house or on streets.
人们可以在诸如咖啡店和街道的公共场合谈论任何事情。
There people read newspapers and talked about politics and military matters.
人们在这些地方看报纸，谈论政治和军事。
It is a great sign of pubic freedom.
这是公共自由的重要标志。

RL.title: UK Population and Nationalist Party 英国人口与民族政党

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: There are 3 million Scottish people and 5 million Welsh people.
苏格兰和威尔士分别有 3 百万和5 百万人口。
London has the population of 7 million, which is nearly the total of Scottish and Welsh.
伦敦有 7 百万人口，几乎是苏格兰和威尔士的总和。
The reason is that UK lack a National Party.
造成人口数量差别的原因是英国缺乏一个国家党。
Scottish Nationalist Party, Welsh Nationalist Party and London Nationalist Party are independent from each other and have many differences.
苏格兰民族党、威尔士民族党和伦敦民族党都相互独立，而且有很多不同政见。

RL.title: Increased Productivity 生产力提高

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The development of technology during Industrial Revolution has increased productivity.
工业革命时期技术的发展提高了生产力。
Thus, there is more output for every unit of input, which reduce cost significantly.
因此每单位投入会有更多的产出，从而降低成本。
For example, the cost of computers was relatively high due to the high cost of semiconductors.
比如，之前电脑的价格相对较高，因为半导体的价格较高。
With increased productivity, the cost of computer parts goes down and computers become cheaper.
因为提高了生产力，电脑零部件的成本降低，电脑也就卖得更便宜了。

RL.title: Wages, Consumption and Household Debt 工资消费和债务增长

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Wages have only grown for 5%.
工资仅仅增长了5%。
However, people ’ s consumption has increased by 15% and household debt has increased by 40%.
但是，消费却增长了 15%，而贷款增加了40%。
The increase in consumption is not due to increasing wages, but is due to household debt because people spend a lot of money at home.
消费的增长不是因为工资增长，而主要是因为贷款增加，因为我们平时在家里的花销变大了。

RL.title: Poverty in Rural Areas 偏远地区的贫困问题

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: We should focus more on rural poverty rather than urban.
我们应该关注偏远地区的贫困问题，而不是城市的。
Poverty in rural areas in Vietnam, India and Zimbabwe leads to environmental problems, including water pollution, sanitation of drinking water, indoor smoke and gas emissions.
越南、印度和津巴布韦的偏远地区贫困问题导致了很多环境问题，包括水污染、饮用水的卫生为题、室内煤烟和气体排放。
We need to address poverty because it can reduce global poor population on the one hand and poverty rate in urban areas on the other because 75% poor people live in rural areas.
我们应该解决贫困问题，它一方面可以减少全球贫困人口，还可以降低城市的贫困率，因为75% 的贫困人口居住在城市中。

RL.title: The Dissociation a of Personality (Morton Prince) 人格分裂

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Morton Prince is an American physician and psychologist.
莫顿·普林斯是美国的内科医生和心理学家。
In his book The Dissociation of a Personality, the character Christine Beauchamp developed several personalities, B1, B2 and B3.
在他的书《人格分裂》中，主人公克里斯汀发展出了多种人格：B1， B2，和B3.
Hidden memory exists between the three personalities. B3 knows the existence of B2 and B1, while B2 knows the existence of B1, and B1 knows neither.
在这三个人格之间隐藏着一部分记忆。B3 人格知道 B2 和 B1 人格的存在，B2 只知道B1 人格的存在，而 B1 人格并不知道其他两个人格的存在。
The strongest personality accounts for most of the time and will take over the others and become the main personality at the end.
最强的人格会占据大多数时间，并且最后会取代另外两个人格，成为主要人格。
The case study is helpful for crime investigation and hallucination treatment.
这本书中的案例分析对犯罪调查和幻觉治疗有帮助。

RL.title: Underwater Antares Detectors 水下探测器

blocks.p: 配图：海上左边有一艘船，海底有鱼，可以远程观察鱼
注：Antares [æn'tεəri:z] 专有名词

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Underwater Antares Detector is a camera installed in a cage under water to monitor fishes.
水下探测器 Antares 是安装在水下笼子里，用来探测鱼的装置。
It is a remote technology system and researchers can monitor fishes on their computers in universities.
它有远程控制技术，因此研究员可以在大学的电脑中监测鱼的行为。
The camera can detect surrounding environments and fish, which help find out what they eat and what they don’t eat.
这个摄像头可以探测鱼和其周围的环境，观测它们吃什么和不吃什么。
So based on what the detector shows, researchers can decide when to stop feeding to save time and labor.
根据探测器的显示结果， 研究员可以决定何时停止对鱼进行喂食，这样可以节省时间和人力。

RL.title: Earth and Mars 地球与火星

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: There are many similarities between Earth and Mars.
地球和火星有许多相似之处。
Both of them have polar caps and atmospheres and are in water climate.
他们都有极地冰冠和大气层，而且都有水环境。
The Earth has ocean, while Mars has ice.
地球上有海洋，火星上有冰。
In preparing for the Phoenix Mission, scientists have done Antarctica trial runs.
在“凤凰计划”的准备过程当中，科学家已经在南极洲做了试验。
They have also dug trenches, collected samples of ice-soil boundary.
并且，他们已经挖了沟壕，并在冰与土的交界处取了样。

pairs: A hadron collider uses underground tunnels, which is 27km long.
强子对撞机使用地下隧道，长 27 千米。
It can generate 7TEV release energy to cause 14,000 times collision.
它可以释放 7 兆电子伏的能量，造成1 万4 千次碰撞。
With proton lights, particles can be released with 1,000,000 times a second.
在质子灯的帮助下，每秒可以释放1 百万粒子。
The ultimate operating temperature is 1.9 Kelvin colder than 2.7 Kelvin, which is the absolute zero of outer space.
太空的绝对零度是 2.7 开尔文，而最后的运行温度比其低1.9 开尔文。
Large Hadron Collider helps to have a better understanding of the universe in the early history.
大型强子对撞机帮助我们更好地理解早期的宇宙。

blocks.p: theories in particle physics and high-energy physics.

RL.title: Practice 刻意练习

blocks.p: 配图片：一个小女孩在拉小提琴

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Talent is closely related to practice.
天赋和练习事密不可分的。
But learning music and mathematics need different kinds of practice.
但是学习音乐和学习数学需要不同的练习。
If you want to be a great violinist, you need thousands of hours of practice.
如果你想成为小提琴家，你需要练习几千个小时。
But if you want to learn mathematics, you need to find your weaknesses and practice accordingly.
但是你想学习数学，你需要查漏补缺，然后做相应的练习。
For example, if you are weak at algebra ( 代 数 ), you practice algebra.
比如，如果你代数不好，那就练习代数。
Even geniuses have to spend far more time to practice to succeed, so there is no need to be ashamed to practice.
就算是一个天才，也需要花很多时间去练习才能获得成功，所以不要因为需要练习而感到羞耻。

RL.title: Cloud 云

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The formation process of clouds need particles in the atmosphere.
云的形成过程需要空气中的微小颗粒。
Sea salt is an effective element to form clouds.
海盐是形成云的有效物质。
As you go inland, other sources can form clouds more effectively than sea salt.
在内陆地区，其他物质比海盐更能形成云朵。
Cloud has many functions. It reflects back the light to keep things cooler in our planet.
云有许多功能。它可将光线反射回去，使得地球的温度不至于太高。
However, when more pollutants go into cloud, they have an impact on water patterns and precipitation.
但是，当很多污染物进入云层，他们可以影响降雨的形式和降雨量。

RL.title: Aristotle’s Rhetoric 亚里士多德的《修辞学》

blocks.p: 配图：如上，近似图

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Aristotle (['æristɔtl]) in his work Rhetoric (['retərɪk]) reveals how truth is related to rhetoric.
亚里士多德在他的著作《修辞学》里，揭示了真理与修辞的关系。
He believes that truth and rhetoric is different.
他认为真理和修辞是不同的。
Rhetoric is the body, while truth is the spirit, the soul.
修辞好比身体，而真理好比精神和灵魂。
Though some people are rational, they do not understand truth.
尽管很多人能保持理性，但他们并不理解真理。
Therefore, in his view, we should use rhetoric to help people to understand truth.
因此，他认为我们应该运用修辞来帮助人们理解真理。
If you want to make people get into truth, you have to use tricks because truth itself is abstract.
如果你想让某人理解真理，那么你要用一些窍门，因为真理本身是抽象的。

人类消耗了可持续发展下应该消耗的自然资源的1.2 倍多。
Each country should record their carbon footprint.
每个国家都应该记录自己的碳足迹。
Australian average Ecological Footprint of 7.7 global hectares per person.
澳洲的平均生态足迹是每人 7.7 全球性公顷。（全球性公顷是生态足迹的单位）

RL.title: Infinite Monkey Theorem 无限猴子定理

如果给猴子纸和笔，让他们拼写 monkey 这5 个字母，他们很可能只能在上面乱写。

近几年其出生率已经讲到历史最低点，为1.1%-1.2%。

当政府开始管理博客的留言，人们又认为他们的言论自由被政府操控了，违背了最初开博客的初衷。
