RL.title: Climate Change 气候变化

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Some adverse effects of climate changes change agricultural production because some lands are unsuitable for growing crops.
气候变化的负面影响将改变农业因为一些土地会变得不适宜耕种。
Millions of people will face hunger in Africa in the near future.
几百万非洲人在不远的将来将面临饥荒。
It is difficult for developing countries to deal with climate change due to their financial status and other issues.
发展中国家因为财务和其他问题无法解决气候变化问题。
The climate change has devastating effects on world economy because it leads to extreme weather conditions such as floods and hurricanes
气候变化会对世界经济产生毁灭性的影响，因为它会导致诸如洪水和飓风这样的极端天气。
As a result, it leads to a continuous decline in food supply annually around 10 to 17%.
因此，它会使得每年的食物供应量减少10%到17%。

blocks.p: Some adverse effects of climate changes change agricultural production. Some lands are just merely unsuitable for growing crops. There will be millions of people facing hunger in Africa in the near future. Climate change will result in less production and less food. It is difficult for developing countries to deal with climate change due to their financial status and other issues. There are many people living in hunger especially in Africa. The climate change has devastating effects on world economy. The tropical areas on earth are dry and hot, and are originally not suitable for food production. The change of climate leads to extreme weather conditions such as floods and hurricanes, which exacerbates the food production issues. As a result, it leads to a continuous decline in food supply annually around 10 to 17%. And this trend is perceived to be continuing in the future by 2070. The regions suffering the most will be some African countries.

RL.title: Australian Cities 澳洲的主要城市

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Australia ’ s location is important for the world ’ s exports, and its international trade is also important.
澳洲对于全球出口业至关重要，它的国际贸易也非常重要。
Since all towns are scattered around in Australia, people spend huge expenses for transportation when using trains and ferries.
由于澳洲的城镇都比较分散，人们花很多钱在交通上，比如火车和渡轮。
The Australian people are mainly living in five cities: Melbourne, Sydney, Perth and Brisbane and Adelaide.
澳洲人主要居住在五大城市：墨尔本，悉尼，珀斯，布里斯班和阿德莱德。
Although Perth is one of the most isolated cities in the world, most large companies such as Telstra and Qantas are both based there.
尽管珀斯是全世界最偏远的城市之一，很多诸如 Telstra 和 Qantas 这样的大公司都设在那里。

blocks.p: Australia’s location is important for the world’s exports, and its international trade is also important. Since Australia has a large territory with vast, uninhabited areas, all towns are scattered around. This leads to huge expenses for transportation when using trains and ferries. The government also have to pay large amounts for its telecommunications to build up the catching between these regions. The Australian people are mainly living in five cities: Melbourne, Sydney, Perth and Brisbane and Adelaide. The most special one is Perth, which is one of the most isolated cities in the world. However, this does not affect its state to be one of the largest cities in Australia. Most large companies, like the two leading companies, Telstra and Qantas, they are both based in Perth.

RL.title: Benefits of Migration 移民的好处

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Economists calculated that removing all immigration controls would double the size of the world economy.
据经济学家计算，去除移民控制政策讲使世界经济增长一倍。
Even a small relaxation of immigration controls would lead to disproportionally big gains.
甚至使很小的政策宽松都可以带来巨大的收益。
It's not just the migrants themselves who gain, it's the countries they come from.
不仅仅使移民他们自己获益，还有他们自己的国家。
Migrants from poor countries send money home through formal or informal channels, which go straight into the pockets of local people to pay for food, clean water and medicines.
来自贫穷国家的移民通过正式或非正式的渠道，将钱寄往自己的国家，这些钱直接到达当地人的手里，用来支付食物、干净的饮用水和药品。

blocks.p: Now the economists calculated, it's a back-of-the-envelope（粗略的）calculation, that removing all immigration controls would double the size of the world economy, and even a small relaxation of immigration controls would lead to disproportionally big gains. Now from an ethical point of view, it's hard to argue against a policy that will do so much to help people that are much poorer than ourselves. The famous Rand Study reckons that a typical immigrant who arrives in US ends up with $20,000 a year, that's rough. It's not just the migrants themselves who gain, it's the countries they come from. Already, the migrants from poor countries working in rich countries send home around 200 billion dollars a year, through formal channels, and about twice as that through informal channels. And that compares to the neat a hundred million dollars that Western governments give in aid. These remittances are not wasted on weapons or siphoned（抽取）off into Swiss bank accounts; they go straight into the pockets of local people. They pay for food, clean water and medicines, they help kids in school, they help start up new business.

RL.title: Shy Fish 害羞的鱼

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Shy individuals actually prefer to follow fish that are similarly timid.
害羞的鱼更喜欢跟着性格跟他们一样胆小的鱼。
But bold follower fish did not seem to care which leader they followed.
但是大胆的鱼不在乎他们鱼群的首领是谁。
The bold fish did lead more expeditions over the course of the experiment than their more retiring friends.
在实验中，大胆的鱼领导鱼群的次数要比那些不善社交的鱼要多。
When offered a choice of leaders, sticklebacks prefer to follow individuals whose personality matches their own.
如果给他们选择，棘鱼会更愿意追随性格跟他们相似的鱼。
But bolder individuals may be able to impose their leadership simply through greater effort even among shy followers.
但是就算是在害羞的鱼群当中，大胆一些的鱼也会花精力给他们施加领导力，使它们跟随它。

blocks.p: When you think of a leader, you may think of an individual who is above all bold. But a new study of fish called stickleback（棘鱼）shows that shy individuals actually prefer to follow fish that are similarly timid.

Researchers had trios（三人组）of sticklebacks with known personalities play follow the leader. The fish were placed in a tank that had some plastic plants at one end and some food hidden at the other. In some of the groups, a bold fish and a shy fish acted as leaders, while another shy fish followed. And in other groups, it was a bold fish that did the following. The researchers recorded whether the follower sallied（出发，动身）forth more frequently with the fish that was behaviorally similar or the one that was different.

What they found is that shy fish were more likely to emerge from under cover when an equally wary （谨慎的，机警的）fellow was already out there. Bold follower fish did not seem to care which leader they followed.

Of course, no matter which fish a stickleback chose to stick with, the bold fish did lead more expeditions over the course of the experiment than their more retiring friends. That’s because the bold fish initiated more trips, regardless of who might be tailing them. The findings are in the journal Biology Letters.

The researchers write that “when offered a choice of leaders, sticklebacks prefer to follow individuals whose personality matches their own, but bolder individuals may, nevertheless, be able to impose their leadership, even among shy followers, simply through greater effort.” We may soon see if such tendencies also hold true in humans, when Americans decide who they’ll follow in November.

RL.title: Happiness and Social Relations 幸福感与社会关系

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Happiness comes from frequency and quality of social relations, which are relations with friends, family and others.
幸福感来自于社会关系的质量和与家人、朋友和其他人的交往频率。
There is evidence that when people feel more satisfied with their social relations, they feel happier.
证据显示当人对自己的社会关系感到满意，他们就会有幸福感。
In turn, when people feel happier, they will feel more satisfied with social relations.
反过来，当人们感到幸福，他们会对自己的社会关系感到更满足。
So some people wonder if their social activities make them happy, or their happy personalities drive them to socialize more with friends and families.
所以一些人想知道到底是社交会懂使他们更幸福，还是自己的幸福力促使他们更多地与他人交往。

RL.title: Language Extinction 语言的消亡

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Many languages are disappearing at a rate that was never seen before in history.
很多语言正在以前所未有的速度在消失。
Urbanization and globalization are the main reasons for this.
城市化和全球化是主要原因。
People who speak small languages are moving to urban areas, where small languages cannot survive.
说小语种的人搬到城市中工作生活，没有机会说小语种。
These people also have to speak global language as well.
这些人也不得不说全球共同语言。
Therefore, small languages can only survive in isolated areas.
因此，小语种在与世隔绝的地方才能生存下来。

RL.title: Aquaculture 水产养殖

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Fish has been the main source of protein for human beings for centuries.
几个世纪以来，鱼肉一直是人类获得蛋白质的主要来源。
One third of the natural fish are caught for meal.
人类捕抓大自然中1/3 的鱼，以所谓食物。
Nowadays, most fishes consumed by people in the market are from aquaculture.
而现在大多数市面上人们吃的鱼都来自于水产养殖。
However, overfishing in some regions brings environmental issues, which needs to be addressed.
但是，一些地区过度捕鱼导致了环境问题，它们亟待解决。

RL.title: Robot 机器人

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Why is it so difficult to make a robot like humans?
为什么制造像人一样的机器人很难？
For some tasks, it is easy and simple for humans to complete, but it is very difficult to ask robots to do what we want.
一些工作对于机器人来说很容易完成，但是另一些工作却很难。
For example, it is hard for robots to recognize colors because they do not have sensory mechanisms.
比如，很难让机器人识别颜色因为他们没有感觉机制。
Artificial intelligence scientists devised a sensor that is implanted to robots to enable them to recognize different colors.
研究人工智能的科学家研究了一种传感器，将它植入到机器人中使其可以识别不同颜色。
The sensor has a camera on it to capture pixels, and then the sensor will transform the pixels into images, which is not as easy as expected.
传感器上有摄像头，能够抓取像素，继而感受器可以将像素转化为图像，但这没有预想得那么简单。

RL.title: Bilingual Education 双语教育

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Many parents use more than one language to communicate with their children at home.
很多家长使用两种语言与自己的孩子沟通交流。
The reason is that the parents themselves can speak more than one language, or that they come from different countries.
因为他们本身掌握两门语言，或者来自不同的国家。
Parents think that using two languages can benefit their children.
家长认为用两种语言与孩子交流对孩子有益。
But actually children will get confused if parents use two languages to explain and talk about the same content.
但事实上如果家长用两种语言与孩子解释一件事情的话，孩子会感到困惑。
If each parent use one language and stick to it, children will won ’ t be confused.
如果家长两人能够分别使用一种语言并坚持，孩子就不会感到困惑。

RL.title: Absolute Zero 绝对零度

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Absolute zero is a temperature at which all natural particles have to vibrational motions, which not attainable.
在绝对零度下，自然界中的所有例子都不再运动。但是绝对零度是无法达到的。
The reason why people do the scientific research of absolute zero is not to obtain a predetermined end.
人们研究绝对零度的原因不是为了达到一个预先设定好的目标。
It is like scientific competition of discovering the things you don ’ t know that exists.
它像一个科学竞赛，去发现人类未知的存在。
This is the beauty of science that scientists love.
这才是科学家们所喜爱的科学的魅力。
We are not focusing on the goal of the experiment, but the results.
我们并不关注实验的目标，而是其结果。（原句）

RL.title: Aging Population 人口老龄化

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The demography has changed a lot as human’s life expectancy increases.
人类寿命延长改变了人口结构。
As the world population grows, the problem of aging population has become more serious.
随着世界人口的增长，老龄化问题变得越来越严重了。
In the past, the population of over 65 years old was 3% in America; now it is 14% and will reach 22% by 2030.
过去，美国超过65 岁的人口占总人口的 3%，现在是 14%，到2030 年会是22%。
The situation is the same in Japan and Germany. Germany will be 28% and Japan will be even worse.
日本和德国的情况一样，德国会是28%， 而日本会更糟糕。
Aging problem is closely related to industrialization.

RL.title: Biology 生物学

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The definition of biology is that it is the study of life in living organisms.
生物学的定义是：对于有生命的有机体的研究。
The scientific definition of an organism is a living thing, such as plants and grass.
而对于有机体的科学定义是一个活着的生命，例如植物和草。
But things get complicated when we are trying to answer the question “What is life ” , because everyone has a different definition.
但是当我们试图回答“什么是生命”的时候，问题会变得很复杂，因为每个人对生命的定义不同。
So, before biology was invented, scientists needed to agree on the definition of life.
因此，在生物学出现之前，科学家首先需要在生命的定义这个问题上达成共识。

blocks.p: 真题原
文：

Welcome to your very first tutorial in biology. Now, in this video series, what I want to do is I want to talk to you guys about many different topics concerning biology. For example, I want to talk to you guys about DNA and genetics in cells, in bacteria, in life and a whole bunch of interesting stuff. But since this is the very first video, I think what we should do in this video is just stick with the very basics. And the first thing I want to do is talk to you guys about what is biology. So, let’s go ahead and answer that question. And the definition of biology is this: the study of life in living organisms. All right, that makes sense up to a certain point up until organisms because you may have heard of organisms before. And you may have your own definition, but the scientific definition of an organism is a living thing. Well, that’s easy. We know what living things are… I’m a living thing, er…plants, grass is a living thing. My puppy named old Dan, cutest puppy ever by the way, is a living thing, but whenever we talk about living things, believe it or not, things get kind of complicated because then you have to ask yourself “what is life”. Well, of course, if you ask your grandma or your best friend or even if you ask a philosopher “What is life”, everyone is gonna give you kind of a different definition of their outlook on life. However, whenever scientists and biologists were first deciding, you know what, “What is life?”, that’s the problem they had. Everyone had their own separate definition of life itself. So, what they needed to do before biology was even invented, which is, of course, the study of life is scientists needed to agree on the definition of life.

RL.title: London’s Fog 伦敦的雾

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Turner painted one of the earliest pictures of London ’ s fog in the 1835 painting, the Thames above Waterloo Bridge.
Turner 1835 年的画《滑铁卢桥上的泰晤士河》第一次描绘了伦敦的雾霾。
The bridge is the central element, and it's partly obscured by the steam and smoke which rises from both sides of the river.
桥是这幅画的主要元素，它被两边从河上冒出的蒸气和烟笼罩，在画中若隐若现。
We can also see a shot-tower and a steam ship.
我们还可以看到一个发射塔和一艘蒸汽船。
It is a potent essay on the energy and complexity of modern polluted urbanization.
它强有力地描绘了受污染的现代化城市的活力和复杂性。
Smoke represents for a flourishing economy, which brings employment and food on tables, but also the dirt and pollution associated with the fumes.
烟象征了繁荣的经济，不仅带来了就业和温饱，也带来了垃圾和污染。

blocks.p: 真题原
文： Turner
not

surprisingly, painted one of the earliest pictures of London’s fog in the 1835 painting, the Thames above Waterloo Bridge. Turner is a trueborn Londoner, is advertising his familiarity with London’s air problem by putting smoke and atmospheric pollution at its center. And as you can see, in here, the bridge is the central elements which is a theme that’s later taken up by Monet. And it's partly obscured by the steam and smoke which rises from both sides of the river. Here, we see a shot-tower. I think you can just about to see it, which was constructed in 1826. Do you know what shot-towers are? They produce shot for guns, ammunition. And they were very smoky, one of the more smoking industries. But it's barely visible, as you can see, as are the various industries on the Lambeth side of the river. There's, on this side, there's a steam ship about to dock or preparing to leave, its black smoke thrusting up to join the kind of swirling arc of smoke there. William Rodner sees this painting as a potent essay on the energy and complexity of modern polluted urbanization. Smoke, I think, here represents for a flourishing economy, which brings employment and food on tables, but also the dirt and pollution associated with the fumes. All seems to be tainted by sulfurous yellow.

RL.title: Animal Behavior Ver.2 动物行为版本二

blocks.p: 配视频：中间会出现一张PPT，如上图

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: There are two fundamental questions about animal behaviour. Proximate questions are those concerned with the mechanisms that bring about behavior and ultimate questions are those concerned with the evolution of behaviour.
关于动物行为有两个基本问题。一个是与产生行为的机制相关，一个与行为进化相关。
For proximate, how does the behaviour develop and secondly what causes the behaviour.
第一个问题往下细分，是指行为是如何产生以及如何发展的。
For ultimate, you can ask how did the behaviour evolve, and secondly what is the adaptive significance of the behaviour。
第二个问题往下细分，是指行为是如何进化以及这种适应性的重要性。
Together these comprise what are called Tinbergen's four questions about animal behaviour, who was one of the founding fathers of the study of animal behaviour。
加在一起就构成了 Tinbergen 关于动物行为的四个问题，他是动物行为研究的奠基人之一。

blocks.p: 参考答案：

We can ask two fundamental questions about animal behavior, they referred to as proximate and ultimate. Proximate questions are those concerned with the mechanisms that bring about behavior; ultimate questions are those concerned with the evolution of behavior. We can divide the proximate and ultimate questions into two sub-questions. For proximate, how does the behavior develop and secondly what causes the behavior. For ultimate, you can ask how did the behavior evolve, and secondly what is the adaptive significance of the behavior, what's its purpose. Together these comprise what are called Tinbergen's four questions about animal behavior. Niko Tinbergen was one of the founding fathers of the study of animal behavior. These questions represent the different ways of studying animal behavior and understanding the difference between those four questions are fundamental to understanding behavior and indeed the whole of biology. How do we study animal behavior? Well that depends
on
the
type
of
question we’re hoping to answer.

RL.title: Taxonomy 分类学

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: Taxonomy is how scientists classify organisms into different groups based on the characteristics that they share.
分类学的定义是，科学家按照有机体共同的特性，将他们分成不同的群体。
US Postal Service is a good example.
这类似于美国的邮政系统。
If we want to send a letter to someone, we address it to the nation or kingdom, then to their states, cities, street number, apartment complex and finally their name.
如果我们想要将信件送达某人，我们要先送至国家或王国，再到州、城市、街号、公寓楼，最后通过名字送达。
In the same way scientists use a taxonomy chart to pinpoint a living creature and organism and how it relates to everything else in the world.
用同样的方式，科学家用分类图来精确查找某一个生物或有机体，并获知它与地球上其他有机体的关系。

blocks.p: Welcome to today's lesson. We’re continuing with our study of taxonomy. Taxonomy is how scientists classify organisms into different groups based on the characteristics that they share. So, for instance, a good way to think about taxonomy is the US Postal Service. If we want to send a letter to someone, we first start off by addressing it to the nation they are in. By default, we usually assume that’s America but it doesn't have to be, could be England or Costa Rica or Spain. You put their nation or their kingdom. Then within that kingdom, you address it to a slightly more specific level, their states. So, for instance, South Carolina would be the same as a phylum（门）. And within that state, you would address it to their city and then to their street number, the street they live on. Then you would address it to say their apartment complex and within that complex, you'd address it by their last name to their family and then finally their first name to the specific person you want to get it to, and in that way, we’re able to weed out all the 400 million people we don't want to send our letter to in America and pinpoint the exact person we want the letter to reach. And in the same way scientists use a taxonomy chart to pinpoint a living creature and organism and how it relates to everything else in the world.

RL.title: Arctic and Antarctic 北极与南极

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: The Arctic at the top of the earth and the Antarctic at the bottom, which are polar regions.
北极在地球的顶部，南极在底部，他们都是极地。
The Arctic was named after the Greek word for bear the little and great bear constellations that can be seen in the sky.
北极的名称来自于希腊语，因在其上空可以看到小熊星座。
These regions are opposite in many ways other than just their names and their location on the globe,
除了在名字和位置上相反，这两个地区还有很多相反的地方。
The Arctic is actually ocean surrounded by land,
北极其实是被大陆包围的海洋。
Surprisingly, a lot of people don’t realize that this isn't actually land. The north pole isn't on land. It's just one big ocean.
令人惊讶的是，很多人并不知道这点。其实北极不是陆地，而是一个大洋。

blocks.p: So, when we talk about the polar regions, just to clarify exactly what we mean. And we have, first of all, the Arctic at the top of the earth and the Antarctic at the bottom. And so the Arctic was named after the Greek word for bear. Now surprisingly it's not after the polar bears that live in the Antar… live in the Arctic and based… it's after the little and great bear constellations that can be seen in the sky. Now the Greeks also hypothesize that there would be the Anti-arctic, which is how we get the name Antarctica and of course it wasn't discovered until much later on. Now these regions are opposite in many ways other than just their names and their location on the globe, and so if we look at the arctic first of all, and the Arctic is actually ocean surrounded by land, and so you can see here this is the UK down here and this kind of Russia and then American Canada around here, and so there is a bit of land cover in our ice on the top in the Arctic, which is Greenland here. But mostly all this area here. Surprisingly, a lot of people don’t realize that this isn't actually land. The north pole isn't on land. It's just one big ocean.

RL.title: Sugar 糖

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: There's sugar in a lot of foods where you don’t expect it.
有很多食物含糖量很高，但你并不知道。
Of course, there's lots of sugar in things that are sweet such as donuts or ice cream.
当然，甜食中含有很多糖分，比如甜甜圈和冰激凌。
But there are other places where you see it and you don't necessarily expect it.
但是其他时候你知道食物中含糖，但不一定知道糖分很高。
For example, there is much sugar in peanut butter and beef stew as ingredients.
比如，在花生酱和炖牛肉中，糖分含量就很高。

blocks.p: 参考答案：

There's sugar in a lot of foods where you don’t expect it. Of course, there's lots of sugar in donuts or ice cream, or pastries, or other things that are sweet, candy of course, but there are other places where you see it and you don't necessarily expect it. So as an example: peanut butter. Here’s a list of ingredients from Skippy Peanut Butter and you see that sugar is the second most common ingredient. So you may know from reading food labels that these ingredients in any food labels that are listed in order of how much there is in the food itself, so sugar comes right after peanuts. Here's another example, beef stew, you wouldn't necessarily expect to find sugar in beef stew but it's there. Now it's down the list of ingredients, it's actually toward the end, but if you look at the marketing of this and look at the can, it says, there’s fresh potatoes and carrots, but actually there’s more sugar in this than there is carrots. And so you wouldn't eat something like beef stew when you expect to find this to be the case.

RL.title: Civilization and Art 文明与艺术

sections.label: 讲座要点 · 中英对照

pairs: We can't have a civilization that doesn't have art.
一个文明不能没有艺术。
A society has built to observe itself and the sophistication of the great civilizations were their ability to look at themselves.
一个社会建立起来，是用来观察我们自己的，而文明的复杂程度显示了人们看待自己的能力。
The producers of art and culture with mirror back to the core of the society allows a society to do that.
文化和艺术的创作者就像镜子一样，使得上述观察和看待自己的需求得以实现。
Art is the vehicle through which we understand that.
艺术也是我们理解和看待自己的工具。
If art were taken away, there would be no such mirror to look at the world in a completely different way.
如果没有艺术，我们就没有这面镜子了，也就无法透过镜子用不同的方式看待世界了。

blocks.p: I have said before that you can't have a civilization that doesn't have art. When we think about the great civilizations historically, all of them had a great production of culture and art because a society has built to observe itself and the sophistication of the great civilizations were their ability to look at themselves. And what allows a society to do that are the producers of art and culture with mirror back to the core of the society. Exactly what is being produced at that moment? How people are thinking of themselves and how individuals are relating to the social structure at that time? Art is the vehicle through which we understand that. Were you to take away art, what would be that mirror? How would we see what we were about? How would we understand what was going on in Paris at the time of the Impressionists when people were learning to see in a completely different way (in) pre-cinematography（前电影艺术）period. All of these things are just emerging and here are people looking at the world in a very different way, which was considered so radical at the time.

FIB-L.title: William Shakespeare 威廉·莎士比亚

blocks.p: For all his fame and celebration, William Shakespeare remains a mysterious figure with regards to personal history. There are just two primary sources for information on the Bard: his works, and various legal and church documents that have survived from Elizabethan times. Naturally, there are many gaps in this body of information, which tells us little about Shakespeare the man.

The first is now in the collection of the National Gallery in London, and the second is in the Van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam. Van Gogh referred to this work as a repetition the London painting. Laurence Stephen Lowry RBS RA was an English artist. Many of his drawings and paintings depict Pend lebury, Lancashire, where he lived and worked for more than 40 years, and also Salford and its surrounding areas. Lowry is famous for painting scenes of life in the industrial districts of North West England in the mid-20th century. He developed a distinctive style of painting and is best known for his urban landscapes peopled with human figures often referred to as matchstick man. He painted mysterious unpopulated landscapes, brooding portraits and the unpublished "marionette" works, which were only found after his death.

For the first time, Japanese researchers have conducted a real-life experiment that shows how some traffic jams appear for no apparent reason. They placed the 22 vehicles on a single track, and asked the drivers to cruise around at a constant speed of 30 kilometers an hour. At first, traffic moves smoothly, but soon, the distance between cars started to vary and vehicles clumped together at one point on the track, but the jams spread backward around the track, like a shock-wave at a rate of about 20 kilometers an hour. Real-life jams move backward at about the same speed.

Many different types of bar code scanning machines exist, but they all work on the same fundamental principles. They all use the intensity of light reflected from a series of black and white stripes to tell a computer what code it is seeing. White stripes reflect light very well, while black stripes reflect hardly and light at all. The bar code scanner shines light sequentially across a bar code, simultaneously detecting and recording the pattern of reflected and non-reflected light. The scanner then translates this pattern into an electrical signal that the computer can understand. All scanners must include computer software to interpret there bar code once its been entered. This simple principle has transformed the way we are able to manipulate data and the way in which many businesses handle record keeping.
